title: BrokenSleep: Remote Power Timing Attack Exploiting Processor Idle States
problem: Modern processors support multiple C-state (idle) levels with different wake-up latencies; an attacker can remotely detect which C-state a victim processor core is in by measuring network response timing, enabling covert and side-channel communication across nodes without requiring co-location on the same machine.
method: BrokenSleep exploits the deterministic wake-up latency differences between processor C-states (C0 active, C1/C1E/C6 sleep) to encode information in the timing of network responses from a victim server. The attacker sends network requests and measures response latency; the victim's current C-state (determined by its workload idle pattern) is deduced from the latency profile. Both covert channel (data exfiltration across security boundaries without direct network access) and side-channel (keystroke timing inference) variants are demonstrated. The attack affects both Intel and ARM processors, exploiting standard ACPI power management without any microarchitectural vulnerability.

title: CirSTAG: Circuit Stability Analysis on Graph-based Manifolds
problem: Circuit stability (sensitivity) analysis requires numerous time-consuming simulations to estimate how parameter variations (gate sizes, capacitance) impact circuit performance. Existing methods struggle with scalability for large integrated circuits.
method: CirSTAG uses graph neural networks to analyze circuit stability through a spectral framework examining input/output graph manifolds. The method calculates a stability score equivalent to the local Lipschitz constant for each node and edge, considering both graph structure and node feature perturbations. When adjacent nodes on the input manifold map to remote nodes on the output manifold (mapping distortion), this indicates poor GNN stability and identifies critical circuit elements.

title: WarpDrive: GPU-Based Fully Homomorphic Encryption Acceleration Leveraging Tensor and CUDA Cores
problem: GPU-based acceleration of Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is bottlenecked by frequent pipeline stalls from memory-latency-bound Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) operations and by suboptimal utilization of GPU hardware units, leaving both CUDA Cores and Tensor Cores underused for FHE workloads.
method: WarpDrive applies three key optimizations: (1) computation decomposition of NTT that reduces total instruction count by 73% through arithmetic restructuring; (2) fine-grained memory access design that pipelines loads to eliminate 86% of pipeline stalls; (3) a concurrent-execution framework that runs CUDA Cores and Tensor Cores simultaneously within a single NTT kernel — the first such combined use — exploiting both unit types' complementary throughput characteristics. Additionally, intra-ciphertext parallelism is maximally extracted without requiring ciphertext batching.

title: ChipAlign: Instruction Alignment in Large Language Models for Chip Design via Geodesic Interpolation
problem: Chip-specific LLMs like ChipNeMo lack instruction alignment capability, limiting their ability to follow explicit human directives and serve as practical assistant chatbots for hardware design engineers.
method: ChipAlign uses geodesic interpolation in weight space to merge instruction-aligned and chip-specific LLMs without training, fusing weights along the manifold to produce a model that inherits both strong instruction following and chip domain knowledge.

title: GoPIM: GCN-Oriented Pipeline Optimization for PIM Accelerators
problem: ReRAM-based PIM accelerators for GCN training suffer from severe pipeline underutilization due to skewed execution times across GCN stages (aggregation, combination) and skewed degree distributions of graph vertices, causing crossbar resource imbalance.
method: GoPIM employs an ML-based scheme that dynamically allocates ReRAM crossbar resources to the most needed pipeline stages to streamline overall execution and eliminate stage bottlenecks. A selective vertex updating technique interleaves vertex mapping across crossbars to evenly distribute vertices despite skewed degree distributions. These two mechanisms reduce overall execution time while maintaining accuracy. A practical architecture design for GoPIM is also provided.

title: PatLabor: Pareto Optimization of Timing-Driven Routing Trees
problem: Timing-driven routing tree construction traditionally balances wirelength and delay using tunable parameters, but cannot compute full Pareto frontiers; parameter tuning lacks theoretical guidance.
method: PatLabor directly optimizes the Pareto set for timing-driven routing trees. For small-degree nets (up to 9 pins), it computes all Pareto-optimal solutions with provable time complexity and approximation bounds. Algorithm avoids parameter tuning by explicitly exploring delay-wirelength trade-off space.

title: A Fast, Iterative Clock Skew Scheduling Algorithm with Dynamic Sequential Graph Extraction
problem: Clock skew scheduling (CSS) requires extracting timing paths between sequential elements, which dominates runtime in advanced CSS algorithms; sequential graph extraction is the performance bottleneck.
method: Iterative CSS algorithm uses timing propagation to facilitate dynamic sequential graph extraction, avoiding full-graph construction. Comprehensive skew calculation incorporates multiple clock latency constraints. Slack optimization techniques achieve target latencies identified by skew analysis.

title: Performance Prediction of On-NIC Network Functions with Multi-Resource Contention and Traffic Awareness
problem: Co-located network functions (NFs) on SmartNICs suffer performance interference from multi-resource contention (CPU cores, memory bandwidth, DMA engines, queues), but existing performance prediction models lack SmartNIC-specific knowledge and traffic-pattern awareness, yielding poor prediction accuracy for SLA management. Operators cannot efficiently allocate SmartNIC resources without accurate contention-aware performance predictions.
method: The paper develops a performance prediction framework that models SmartNIC-specific resource contention by profiling the interactions between co-located NFs across multiple resource dimensions (CPU, memory, interconnects). The model incorporates traffic awareness by accounting for how arrival patterns and traffic rates influence queuing delays and per-NF throughput under contention. Machine learning or analytical models (details from abstract) are used to predict NF latency and throughput given a resource allocation and traffic profile.

title: Avalanche: Optimizing Cache Utilization via Matrix Reordering for Sparse Matrix Multiplication Accelerator
problem: Sparse Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) accelerators suffer from poor on-chip memory utilization due to irregular memory access patterns; existing designs fail to cache both input matrices efficiently, leading to redundant DRAM accesses and low throughput.
method: Avalanche applies three complementary techniques: (1) Mat-Reorder reorders columns of matrix B to maximize data locality and enable early completion of row computations in matrix A; (2) DP-Evict (Dead-Product Early Eviction) immediately evicts fully-computed intermediate products from on-chip SRAM to reclaim capacity; (3) RM-Caching (Reuse Distance-Aware Matrix Caching) prioritizes retention of matrix B elements with short reuse distances in the on-chip cache. Together these techniques keep both operand matrices resident in a 6.15 mm2 chip with minimal spill-to-DRAM.

title: Hopps: Leveraging Sparsity to Accelerate Automata Processing
problem: Automata processing (AP) workloads execute many finite state machines (FSMs) in parallel over streaming symbol data, but existing AP accelerators suffer poor utilization because most FSMs are inactive (in a non-matching state) for any given input symbol. The irregular, state-dependent activation pattern makes it hard to exploit spatial parallelism efficiently.
method: Hopps exploits the observation that only a sparse subset of FSMs transition on each input symbol. It uses a sparsity-aware representation that tracks only active states across all FSMs and a compressed activation bitmap to skip idle FSMs entirely during each symbol step. The architecture couples this with a tiled SRAM storage layout so that state-transition tables for active FSMs are fetched in bursts, reducing off-chip memory traffic proportional to the active-FSM fraction.

title: Generalizing Reuse Patterns for Efficient DNN on Microcontrollers
problem: DNN inference on microcontrollers is limited by their restricted compute and memory, and existing computation reuse techniques that exploit redundancy in input/activation data are constrained by a narrow definition of reuse patterns, leaving a large portion of potential reuse unexploited.
method: The work introduces generalized reuse, which frames computation reuse in terms of row and column reordering of a matrix view of DNN input or activation maps. By recognizing that different reorderings expose different reuse patterns, the approach dramatically expands the explorable reuse space beyond what prior narrow pattern definitions allow. Two analytical models are developed: one predicts the accuracy impact of a given reuse pattern (approximate computation), and one predicts latency on the target microcontroller. These models enable efficient search over the generalized reuse space to select patterns that best trade off accuracy and speed for a given DNN and hardware.

title: Micro-MAMA: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multicore Prefetching
problem: Independent RL-based prefetchers on each core of a multicore system compete for shared memory bandwidth without coordination, causing each agent to greedily claim excessive bandwidth and converging to sub-optimal system-wide policies. This problem is an instance of the multi-agent credit assignment and non-stationarity challenge in MARL.
method: MAMA uses a two-tier architecture: distributed local multi-armed bandit agents on each core narrow the joint-action search space by selecting among local prefetch aggressiveness options, while a central supervisor agent with global bandwidth visibility learns joint policies that maximize system-wide throughput or fairness. Key local agents receive system-level perspective signals (estimated global bandwidth usage) to discourage actions that harm other cores. The supervisor uses a lightweight bandit over the local agents' reduced action space, avoiding the exponential joint-action blow-up of fully centralized control.

title: Qtenon: Towards Low-Latency Architecture Integration for Accelerating Hybrid Quantum-Classical Computing
problem: Hybrid quantum-classical algorithms are bottlenecked by the decoupled architecture of current quantum hardware systems, which lacks low-latency communication channels and fine-grained software control for tightly coordinating quantum and classical computation. The high round-trip latency between host processor and quantum accelerator prevents real-time feedback loops required by variational algorithms.
method: Qtenon is a RISC-V extended chip implemented in Chisel that tightly couples classical and quantum processing via three hardware components: a unified memory hierarchy serving as a shared communication buffer between the host and quantum accelerators, an efficient quantum controller with dedicated data paths, and a multi-stage processing pipeline that exploits instruction-level parallelism across quantum-classical interaction phases. A custom ISA extension provides instructions for data communication, computation, fine-grained synchronization, and efficient scheduling of quantum-host interaction.

title: Simplifying and Accelerating NOR Flash I/O Stack for RAM-Restricted Microcontrollers
problem: NOR flash file systems for RAM-restricted microcontrollers migrate block-level data organization and wear leveling logic from RAM into flash, introducing fine-grained block-level management that causes frequent index updates and full-device scans. This results in severe I/O amplification that worsens when the management layers are decoupled across the I/O stack.
method: The paper redesigns the NOR flash I/O stack to eliminate the decoupled block-level management abstraction, instead employing coarse-grained, integrated data organization that reduces index update frequency. Wear leveling is restructured to operate at a coarser granularity aligned with the NOR flash erase unit, avoiding the fine-grained scanning overhead. The resulting simplified stack collapses previously separate software layers to reduce coupling and I/O amplification jointly.

title: SeaCache: Efficient and Adaptive Caching for Sparse Accelerators
problem: Sparse tensor accelerators suffer from poor on-chip SRAM utilization because variable-length sparse fibers (rows/columns of nonzero data) do not map cleanly into fixed-size cache blocks, wasting capacity. Theoretically optimal replacement policies (e.g., Belady OPT) require expensive on-chip metadata that consumes significant die area.
method: SeaCache combines three techniques targeting sparse on-demand caches integrated in domain-specific accelerators. First, fiber packing and splitting maps variable-length sparse fibers into fixed-size cache blocks with high utilization by splitting long fibers across multiple blocks and packing short fibers together. Second, a practical replacement policy approximates OPT-like behavior at low implementation cost by exploiting access-pattern regularities in sparse computations. Third, an adaptive space-sharing mechanism dynamically partitions the cache between actual data and replacement policy metadata using a two-phase approach that measures and adjusts the optimal partition ratio at runtime.

title: Security Opportunities and Challenges for Disaggregated Architectures (Invited)
problem: Disaggregated computer architectures separate CPU, memory, storage, and networking into independently managed units communicating over networks, introducing new security attack surfaces and isolation risks.
method: Invited position paper analyzing security aspects of disaggregation across three domains: network fabric (enterprise routing), O-RAN (software-defined radio), and trusted execution environments. Discusses attack surfaces, data exposure, provenance tracking, isolation, and API security.
